persons.note: BORN AT LYONS, FRANCE, 2 NOVEMBER 1803, AND EDUCATED THERE. Andreas: 'He left France in June, 1831, reached St. Louis August 1, of the same year, and was there made a subdeacon. He was ordained at St. Mary's the Barrens by Bishop Rosatti in 1832, and on April 6, 1833, was by the same Bishop ordained priest.' He was sent to Chicago because 'Catholics were increasing in numbers in Chicago, and were becoming desirous' of a priest - a petition answered, not a migration chosen. He was succeeded by Father O'Meara only after 1837, so he is the pastor across the whole scene window.

research_note: THE ONLY CATHOLIC HOUSEHOLD IN THIS PARCEL AND ONE OF ITS BEST-DATED, which is a lopsided result worth stating: St Cyr's own movements are documented to the day while the congregation he came for - the Catholics who were 'increasing in numbers' and petitioned for him - is a body of people this dataset cannot name at all. THAT CONGREGATION IS THE LARGEST SINGLE POPULATION THE INFERRED PHASE HAS TO ACCOUNT FOR on the south side, and the church building is the evidence that it existed. A note for that phase: the lumber for the twenty-five by thirty-five foot church came by scow from St Joseph, Michigan, at $12 per thousand, and Anson Taylor hauled it from the schooner with his own team - three named trades in one sentence about one building.
